name: Namibia
summary_text: Namibia demands real caution from trans visitors. Courts have delivered important rulings (the 2023 Digashu recognition of foreign same-sex marriages; earlier document-change wins for trans people), but same-sex conduct between men technically remains criminalised under the common law (the 2024 High Court declined to strike it, and parliament passed hostile marriage bills), and implementation of pro-LGBT rulings is documented as unsatisfactory (SALC). Windhoek has a small organised community (Equal Namibia); police are unhelpful rather than predatory. For a visitor: enforcement of the old law is essentially nil, but the legal floor is hostile and the politics are deteriorating.

sources.title: To comply or not to comply is not the question
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade op-ed (May 2024, by Daniel Digashu & Anna Mmolai-Chalmers, also published by SALC): 'To comply or not to comply is not the question' — courts in Namibia and Botswana have issued landmark LGBTQI+ rulings (decriminalisation, immigration recognition of foreign same-sex marriages) but government implementation remains unsatisfactory.

UNDP report (Dec 2024) 'African Commission Resolution 275: Ten Years of Advancing LGBT+ Rights in Africa' - regional framework document; Namibia's courts have decriminalised same-sex conduct (2024) and recognised same-sex partners' residency rights, though implementation remains contested.

SALC 'Transgender Rights in Namibia' (2017): constitutional analysis - Article 10 omits gender identity/sexual orientation but 'other status' should include them per the UN Human Rights Committee; section 7B of the Births, Marriages and Deaths Registration Act 81 of 1963 allows gender-marker changes on medical evidence, handled case-by-case and 'not problematic' per the Legal Assistance Centre (2015).

sources.title: Namibia's first LGBT health centre opens in Windhoek - MambaOnline - LGBTQ South Africa online
sources.claim_summary: Mambaonline (May 2018): Namibia's first LGBT health centre opened in Windhoek - the Outreach Health drop-in-centre launched by Out-Right Namibia on IDAHOT, offering mental health and sexual/reproductive health services; ORN Director Friedel Dausab: 'It is a first.'

sources.title: Namibia celebrates LGBTI+ Pride in Windhoek and Swakopmund (Pictures) - MambaOnline - LGBTQ South Africa online
sources.claim_summary: Mambaonline (Dec 2018): Namibia celebrated LGBTI+ Pride in Windhoek and Swakopmund - the Windhoek march (World AIDS Day, #WeAreOne) was called the 'biggest pride event' to date, led by Coded MCC bikers with police escort and a mobile HIV testing clinic.

sources.title: Homophobic Namibian fighters: What the EFF?
sources.claim_summary: Daily Maverick (June 2014): 'Homophobic Namibian fighters: What the EFF?' - a Namibian version of South Africa's Economic Freedom Fighters was launched with identical branding but an explicitly anti-gay stance, unlike the South African original.
